punchline: Johnson & Johnson cut 311 words into granite, and then kept its managers arguing over them.
thirty_sec: Daniel Coyle points to the Johnson & Johnson Credo, 311 words carved in granite at its New Jersey headquarters. When the 1982 Tylenol poisoning hit, the company's answer was in those words. Coyle's point is that managers had been meeting to discuss and challenge it long before.
